brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8%, so there's room in their price

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target the lower end of the market fair band ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps at higher volume, down from the typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit on every sale vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra 2.1% is room to cut price. The market ask for a 28 mm PP cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typically, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (moving from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for part of the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹22.57 L in cash. They borrow money at about 12.19%, so paying early is worth roughly that rate to them — use it to sweeten the price cut ask.

brief.financialLeverage: They're financially healthy — CRISIL A+ credit rating, making money (5.9% profit), and growing fast. Our ₹5.49 Cr spend is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue, so we're a small customer and can't threaten to walk away alone. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, so they feel the squeeze and will value faster payment. They also already stretch their own suppliers to 49d vs 37d peer average, so asking them to give us longer terms is only fair. Push hard on price — their strong rating and higher profit mean they can absorb it — and dangle faster payment to close the gap.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck longer than similar firms
They stretch their own suppliers longer than most
We're a tiny customer to them
They borrow at about 12.19%, so early payment is worth that rate to them
Strong credit rating means low risk they'll fail

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — top second-source candidate with health score B (65/100)

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) at ₹946.50 Cr revenue — strong, profitable, health score B (73/100) — robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging at ₹701.17 Cr revenue — broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: We're only 0.59% of their business, so we have little walk-away power — line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek before you push too hard

They sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.17) — not distress, but not rock-solid either — so don't squeeze so hard you tip them into trouble; frame the ask around a win-win (faster payment for lower price)
The market ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' with only modest headroom — don't anchor to an unrealistic number or they'll walk; stay within the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band at volume
Their interest coverage is 2.94x — comfortable but not huge — so they'll feel the 12.19% borrowing cost and value early payment, but won't panic
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing our price in line with the market fair range and tightening payment terms — you're keeping 5.9% profit vs the industry's 3.8%, so there's room, and we're ready to pay faster to help your cash flow.
